Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, Barangay West Triangle, Quezon City wmv.dilg.qov.ph DILG OPINION No. 89 s. 2022 SEP 09 2022 HON. NILO C. MALANYAON II Vice-Mayor Municipality of Bula Province of Camarines Sur Dear Vice-Mayor Malanyaon II: This has reference to your letter dated 21 July 2022 seeking legal opinion from this Department on the following: I. Whether or not the municipal mayor has the sole authority to approve the hiring of Contract of Service Personnel (CSP) in all offices of the municipality, including that of the office of the vice-mayor / Sangguniang Bayan; and 2. Whether or not an executive order declaring that the municipal mayor has the sole authority to approve the hiring of CSP in all offices of the municipality is valid. Per your representation, the foregoing issues arose after Mayor Amelita A. Ibasco of the Municipality of Bula, Camarines Sur issued Executive Order No. 2022-09 on I July 2022 which declares that the request for authority to hire/renew the contract of service of personnel and consultant shall be addressed to the Local Chief Executive (LCE). You also represented that it requires that the department heads and heads of offices shall submit their request to hire/renew the contracts for approval of the LCE. Also, you stated that EO No. 2022-09 provides that the LCE has the sole authority to approve the authority to hire for renewal of the individual contracts of service personnel. You then stated that Mayor Ibasco anchors her alleged sole authority to approve the contract of service personnel under Sec. 444(1)(ix) of the Local Govemment Code. You further represented that EO No. 2022-09 have encroached your appointing powers as the Vice Mayor under Section 445(a)(2) of the LGC. Hence, the queries. At the outset, we note that your queries appear to be interrelated. Your first query delves on the sole authority of the municipal mayor to approve the hiring of contract of service personnel in all offices of the municipality while the second query pertains to the validity "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

of EO No. 2022-09 issued by the municipal mayor declaring that she has the authority to hire/renew contract of service personnel. Simply put, EO No. 2022-09 is just the document that embodies the sole authority of the municipal mayor to approve the hiring of contract of service personnel in all offices of the municipality. For this, we shall discuss your queries in one (1) discussion. Please be informed that the Department has no authority to declare EO No. 2022-09 invalid. Only the courts can do so upon filing of an appropriate pleading. We would like to reiterate, however, the standing DILG opinion delineating the appointing authorities between the Local Chief Executives and the Vice-Local Chief Executives. In DILG Legal Opinion No. 34 s. 2014, we made a distinction as to the hiring of employees, this wise: a. Employees of the sanggunian and the Office of the Vice-Mayor whose salaries are paid out of the municipal funds; b. Employees of the sanggunian and of the Office of the Vice-Mayor whose salaries are paid out of the funds appropriated for the sanggunian; c. Casual employees in the sanggunian and of the Office of the Vice-Mayor ii. Those provided for in the plantilla of the local government unit concerned and filled up via "appointment"; Those not provided for in the plantilla and hired through job order contracts regardless of the source of funds. As to the employees under letter (a), the Mayor has the authority to appoint them. With regards to the employees under letter (b) and letter (c)(i) the Vice-Mayor has the authority to appoint them. However, with regards to employees under (c)(ii) whose items are not so provided in the plantilla and hired only through the execution of job order contracts regardless of the source of funds, we are of the view that it is the Mayor who has the authority to hire them pursuant to Sections 77 and 444(b)(i)(vi) [in so far as Municipal Mayor is concemed] of the Local Government Code of 1991, to wit: "SECTION 77. Responsibility for Human Resources and Development. — The chief executive of every local government unit shall be responsible for human resources and development in his unit and shall take all personnel actions in accordance with the Constitutional provisions on civil service, pertinent laws, and rules and regulations thereon, including such policies, guidelines and standards as the Civil Service Commission may establish: Provided, That the local chief executive may employ emergency or casual employees or laborers paid on a daily wage or piecework basis and hired through job orders for local projects authorized by the Sanggunian concerned, without need of approval or attestation by the Civil Service Commission: Provided, further, That the period of employment of emergency or casual laborers as provided in this Section shall not exceed six (6) months. " (Emphasis ours) Page 2 of 3

Xxx "Section 444(b)(i)(vi). Upon authorization by the Sanggunian Bayan, represent the municipality in all its business transactions and sign on its behalf all bonds, contracts, and obligations, and such other documents made pursuant to law or ordinance;" (Emphasis ours) Since job orders result to the execution of contract of services and/or job order contracts, it necessarily follows, pursuant to Section 444(b)(i)(vi) of the Local Government Code of 1991, in so far as the Municipal Mayor is concerned, has the authority to hire them. We have attached a copy of the above-mentioned legal opinion for your ready reference. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Very respectfully yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: GAN Unders r tary for Local Government OUSLG/MLWLLLS-LRALLD/lasm/anor copy furnished: ATTY. ANTHONY C.
